findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed the raw steak stored over raw fish, and raw ground pork stored over cooked baked potatoes. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and moved the fish above the the steak and to the side so that fish was not stored below steak, and the ground pork was moved to a lower shelf where it was below raw whole steak and above raw chicken. Ensure that foods are stored properly in order of final cooking temperatures: RTE foods and washed produced (no cooking) on top, followed by unwashed produce, followed by eggs (135 F), then fish (135 F), then whole intact meat (145 F), ground and comminuted meat (155 F), and finally chicken and poultry (165 F) on the bottom shelf.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed that the hot box in the kitchen was not hot holding recently cooked food at 135 F and above: marinara was probed at 130 F and green beans were probed at 125 F. CORRECTED: PIC took all containers back to the oven and stove to reheat them above 165 F and determined that the hot box needed to be turned up higher. Temperatures were remeasured at 151 F (marinara) and 153 F (green beans) and the ambient air temperature of the hot box was measurably hot. Ensure that cooked food items are hot held at internal temperatures of 135 F and below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed that a spray bottle with degreaser solution was unlabeled. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and the spray bottle was labeled immediately. Ensure that all chemicals that are in working containers be labeled to prevent food or surface contamination or improper use.
findings.citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed several single-use containers and single-service articles stored upright where the food-contact surfaces were exposed to contamination from falling debris. CORRECTED: PIC had all items either inverted or placed under a shelf where they would be protected. Ensure all single-service and single-use articles and utensils are protected from contamination during storage, either through a protective container, inversion, or an upper barrier.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed the underside of the shelf above the steam table has accumulated debris from old food splashes. The PIC was notified, and made plans to clean it later and add it to the regular cleaning schedule. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces of equipment are maintained clean of food residues.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Dented cans were observed in dry storage. The observed cans were shown and discussed with the PIC. The cans were removed for discard to correct. Insure package integrity of all cans in the facility moving forward.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: (1) A dirty knife was observed with food debris on the magnetic rack next to the three part sink. (2) A food dicer tool was observed with remaining food debris while stored on top of the ice machine. The PIC was notified and shown both items, and they were moved back to dish to correct. Insure that all food-contact items are completely clean prior to storage to sight and touch at all times.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: A spray bottle with degreaser solution was unlabeled. It is important that all chemicals that are in working containers be labeled to prevent cross contamination or improper use. The PIC was notified and the spray bottle was labeled immediately.
findings.citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Personal items were stored in a metal cooking pan along with a stem thermometer. PIC was shown and the thermometer was washed to correct. Food contact utensils should be stored so that they are not exposed to sources of contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.12(A)(1) and A(3)-(8) Prohibitions. (A) Cleaned and SANITIZED EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES may not be stored: (8) Under other sources of contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The underside of the shelf above the steam table was observed to have accumulated debris from old food splashes. The PIC was notified, and made plans to clean it later at the end of the day, and clean it on a regular schedule. It is important that non-food contact surfaces of equipment are maintained clean.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee was preparing a wrap for a customer using their bare hands. The employee was educated and they washed hands and put on gloves to continue preparing foods. The PIC will be reminding all staff about proper food handling. Ensure that employees always handle ready-to-eat foods with gloves or another barrier.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed the following are not smooth, easily cleanable surfaces:

(1) The caulking to the right of the dish machine is starting to degrade; the caulking must be repaired/replaced to seal the surface to the wall. 

(2) The gasket on the left door of the cookline freezer is not fully attached; the gasket must be repaired/replaced. 

Ensure that the above referenced are smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the salad prep cooler has an accumulation of food residue on the bottom. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the bottom of the salad prep cooler is cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employee was educated on the proper hand washing procedure when the action was observed. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: A half consumed water bottle is observed in the kitchen on a lower shelf next to closed a plastic tub holding clean wrapped utensils. Containers for employees to drink out of should have lids and straws. Designating a storage area away from food and clean utensil storage is optimal. The bottle was discarded in the garbage.

(A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: Inspector observed the floor wall juncture to be soiled in the kitchen. Take care to clean the heavily soiled areas and maintain them clean by sweeping all the way to the wall before mopping. The facility has purchased a small pressure washer to help with this build up. Take care not to shove water under the walls with the pressure washer. Clean and maintain these areas clean especially the area under the dish area and the area to the left of the hand sink on the cook line. 

(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed an employee check their text messages on their watch with gloved hands and then proceed to return to cooking on the grill and food prep. The employee was stopped and coached on correct times to wash hands and proper glove use. The violation is considered corrected at time of inspection. Take every opportunity to coach proper hand washing.

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the base cabinets at the server station to be soiled with soda splash on the outside and leaking soda boxes on the inside. The material is raw wood and is no longer smooth, and nonabsorbent. Repair or replace the base cabinets to meat the requirements of this part. 

4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.
